name: scroll-reveal-css
summary: A grid of cards that fade, grow or slide in one by one as they cross the viewport, on native CSS scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline: view()`) with no JavaScript and no library. Any element opts in with a `data-mogp-motion` attribute, and per-element attributes set where in its time on screen the motion starts and ends, the starting scale and the slide distance. Browsers without scroll-driven animations, and visitors who prefer less motion, see every card in place.

deviations.what: Every `--mogp-*` custom property in the stylesheet is renamed `--fx-mogp-*`.
deviations.why: paw-fx prefixes its custom properties with `--fx-`. The `data-mogp-*` attributes and the `mogp-*` keyframe names are upstream's public API and keep their spelling, so markup written for upstream works unchanged.

deviations.what: The section layout (`.fx-reveal` and its head, grid, card and tag) is appended after the upstream block.
deviations.why: Upstream is an attribute system, not a section, so paw-fx needs markup to put it in. The layout is taken from upstream's own index.html demo page (its card, tag, heading and 12-column grid values) rather than drawn fresh, scoped under `.fx-reveal`, and does not animate.
